name: m5_matexpr_signprint
stressor: shared numeric/format contract across sibling printers: one sign-printing rule (negative coefficient -> '-' / subtraction) must be re-derived identically in 3 independent printer modules; a partial fix prints inconsistently
source_note: Ports sympy issue #14237 'The difference of MatrixSymbols prints as a sum with (-1) coefficient' (https://github.com/sympy/sympy/issues/14237), fixed by PR #14248 'str, latex, pretty: changed MatrixSymbol printing' (https://github.com/sympy/sympy/pull/14248), the basis of SWE-bench instance sympy__sympy-14248 (repo sympy/sympy). The real gold patch edits THREE printer source files consistently -- sympy/printing/str.py, sympy/printing/latex.py, sympy/printing/pretty/pretty.py -- each updating _print_MatAdd (turn a term whose printed form is negative into subtraction, drop a leading '+') and _print_MatMul (pull a leading negative numeric coefficient out as a single '-' sign instead of printing '(-1)*'). The other code printers (ccode/fcode/etc., all subclasses of CodePrinter) are NOT touched for MatAdd/MatMul. Modeled at small scale as a self-contained 'matexpr' package: MatrixSymbol/MatMul/MatAdd algebra (where A - B is MatAdd(A, MatMul(-1, B))) plus StrPrinter/LatexPrinter/PrettyPrinter sharing the buggy contract, with a CodePrinter (C helper-call form) as the distractor that must stay byte-identical.
discriminator: The identical sign/subtraction rule must be implemented three times -- once per printer module -- because the printers do not share a MatAdd/MatMul implementation (only a dispatch base). The fix is not a single edit nor a blanket find/replace: each printer formats products differently ('*' vs space vs dot), and the lookalike CodePrinter has the same method names and the same '_Coeff' handling but must NOT change (its (-1) is a real C-helper argument). A bounded-slice agent holds all three printer files plus the distractor in its working set and applies the rule uniformly; a growing-transcript agent tends to fix one or two printers (commonly leaving pretty or latex on the old '+ '/'(-1)' behavior) or to wrongly edit the code printer, so output is inconsistent across printers and a partial fix still fails verify.
